help.title: Help
help.protocolTypesDesc: Nomos organizes data collection into protocols. Each project uses a single protocol, which defines the forms filled out in the field. Two protocols are currently available:
help.officialProtocolDesc: Nomos's original scientific protocol, developed by the PAISAGEO/UFPE Group for landscape cartography based on Geosystems Theory. It has three fixed modules: Vegetation (with the Küchler Method), Geoecological Constraints (landform, surface cover, and soil) and Environmental Impacts.
help.customProtocolDesc: A form created by the user, with fully configurable sections and fields (text, numbers, photos, audio notes, species lists, and more). It can be exported as a file and imported on another device, making it easy to work as a team.
help.step1Desc: Start by creating a project and choosing the protocol type: Paisageo (landscape cartography) or Custom (customized fields). For custom projects, create or import the protocol before creating the project.
help.step2Title: Prepare the Project for the Field
help.step2Desc: Before heading to the field, prepare the project: add the planned field route, review the area on the map, and build the species catalog (searching online or adding entries manually), among other preparations.
help.step3Desc: In the field, add collection points by automatically capturing GPS coordinates or manually selecting locations on the map.
help.step4Desc: For each point, fill forms according to the protocol and include photos and audio notes to enrich field records.
help.step5Desc: Export the project data in GeoJSON or CSV; photos and audio notes are exported separately, organized by collection point.
help.speciesCatalogDesc: Projects with floristic records have their own species catalog, used to speed up form filling in the field. The catalog is local, but it can be fed with online searches and shared with the team.
help.offlineMapsDesc: View your geospatial data even without internet connection. Perfect for remote areas.
help.multiProtocolDesc: Nomos's core is protocol-agnostic: collect data with the Paisageo scientific protocol or build your own custom protocol, with the same field, map, and export flow.
help.dataExportDesc: Export data in GeoJSON (spatial) and CSV (tabular); photos and audio notes are available separately, in a package organized by point.
help.mediaCaptureDesc: Capture photos and audio notes at each collection point to enrich field data with visual evidence and local context.
help.useDescriptiveNames: Use descriptive names for your projects
help.tipIncludePhotos: Include photos of points and surroundings to improve interpretation
help.tipRecordAudio: Use audio notes for observations that are too long to type in the field
help.tipCheckLocation: Review the point on the map and confirm GPS before saving
help.tipReviewBeforeSave: Check required fields before finalizing each survey
help.needMoreHelpDesc: Check the complete documentation, report issues, or contribute to the project on the official GitHub repository.

about.title: About the Project
about.subtitle: Environmental Inventories
about.description: Nomos is an app for environmental inventories. Its conception arose from a Master's research project aimed at digitizing and operationalizing a field data collection methodology for landscape mapping. In this first version, the app implements the Paisageo Protocol — a structured approach for the systematic recording of environmental information in the field — and also allows the creation of custom protocols, making it possible to adapt data collection to other methodologies and research purposes.
about.author: Author
about.institutionName: Federal University of Pernambuco (UFPE) - Geography Graduate Program (PPGEO)
about.researchGroupsName: Intertropical Landscape Dynamics Research Laboratory (INTERTRÓPICOS) and the Research Group in Geography and Conservation in Tropical Landscapes (PAISAGEO - UFPE)
about.techDatabaseDesc: SQLite 3.45 providing local storage for projects
about.techArchitectureDesc: 100% offline app (data stored locally via SQLite), with an extensible plugin/protocol-based architecture
about.licenseDesc: This project is open source under the GNU GPL v3.0 license (copyleft). You may use, study, modify, and redistribute the software, including commercially, provided derivative works are distributed under the same license with source code available.
about.institutionalCreditsDesc: Nomos is supported by institutional and scientific entities linked to research, funding, and academic production.
